brief.topic: Log one LLM call so you can debug it next month
brief.audience: PMs and engineers running LLM features in production
constraints: Log values are fictional; time comparison is illustrative and labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: To explain or reproduce a bad AI answer you need the prompt version, model, input, retrieved documents, exact output, latency/tokens and the user's next action logged for every call.

hooks.text: You can’t fix an answer you didn’t log.

hooks.text: A user says the AI was wrong. Now what?
hooks.notes: Relatable, but the answer is less clear.

caption.opening: When a user reports a bad answer, you need to see exactly what the model saw and said. Without a log, you’re guessing.
body:
Log these for every call:
→ Prompt version
→ Model
→ Input: the user message and context sent
→ Retrieved document IDs
→ The exact output shown
→ Latency and tokens
→ What the user did next (edited, copied, retried, left)
Handle user inputs with care: redact sensitive data and set a retention limit.
(Log values in the reel are made up; 2 days vs 20 minutes is illustrative.)

claims.text: Logging prompt version, model, input, retrieved documents, exact output, latency/tokens and the user's next action per LLM call makes bad answers reproducible and explainable.
About 2 days to find the cause of a bad answer without a call log vs about 20 minutes with one.
